Data on scales as a dense array

Source: R/array.R
as_scale_array.Rd

Reshapes a long table into an array whose dimensions are the scale's axes, in the order the product declares them, with the units as dimnames.

as_scale_array(data, x, value = NULL, frames = NULL, fill = NA, limit = 1e+07)

as_scale_table(a, x, value = "value", frames = NULL, drop_na = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A long table with one column per axis key plus the value column. Lazy inputs are materialised – an array is a dense in-memory object by definition.

x

A NestedScale or ScaleProduct.

value

Name of the value column. Defaults to the single numeric column that is not a key.

frames

Optional named list giving the frame each axis is keyed at; defaults to each axis's atom frame.

fill

Value for cells the data does not cover.

limit

Refuse to allocate more than this many cells.

a

An array produced by as_scale_array() (or shaped like one).

drop_na

Omit cells the array does not cover, rather than emitting them as rows with NA values.

Value

An array with one dimension per axis.

as_scale_table() returns a data.frame: one column per axis key, plus the value column.

Examples

p <- scale_product(a = scale_example(), b = scale_example2())
d <- merge(
  data.frame(unit = c("U1", "U2")),
  data.frame(period = c("p1", "p2"))
)
d$v <- 1:4
as_scale_array(d, p, value = "v")
#>      b
#> a     p1 p2 p3 p4
#>   U1   1  3 NA NA
#>   U2   2  4 NA NA
#>   U3  NA NA NA NA
#>   U4  NA NA NA NA
#>   U5  NA NA NA NA
#>   U6  NA NA NA NA
#>   OTH NA NA NA NA
as_scale_table(as_scale_array(d, p, value = "v"), p, value = "v")
#>   unit period v
#> 1   U1     p1 1
#> 2   U2     p1 2
#> 3   U1     p2 3
#> 4   U2     p2 4
